requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: busybox-extras was installed to obtain an httpd applet, /srv/localrepo/x86_64 was populated with tree-2.2.1-r0.apk and dependencies plus a generated APKINDEX.tar.gz, and busybox-extras httpd was started on port 8080 serving that directory. Direct HTTP 200 responses to the index were observed both during the test and after the later reboot.

requirements.requirement: Confirm usual remote repositories are unreachable before/while installing from the local repo
requirements.summary: dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org was redirected to 127.0.0.1 via /etc/hosts; a direct curl to the remote index returned exit 7/000 (connection refused) and `apk update` reported 'Connection refused' for both the main and community remote repos, directly demonstrating remote unreachability.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repo while remotes are unreachable
requirements.summary: With the remote still blocked, `apk add --repository http://10.100.52.10:8080 --allow-untrusted tree` succeeded, and tree was verified functional (`tree --version`, `apk info -e tree`). An earlier attempt with an incorrect repository path (cmd-5f88c5346b4c4507) failed cleanly with no lasting package-state damage (post-executor package-health check shows only the pre-existing chrony.drift entry) and was immediately corrected.

requirements.requirement: Restore normal remote-repository access after the test (implicit reversibility of the simulated outage)
requirements.summary: /etc/hosts was restored from its backup; a direct curl to the remote CDN returned HTTP 200 and `apk update` succeeded against the real remote repositories again, confirming the simulated outage did not leave lasting network/config damage.

requirements.requirement: (Independent) Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id c30a625a-...(matches the fixed before-prepare snapshot), with httpd running, repo reachable, and tree installed. A native reboot was acknowledged and the node became unreachable across several polls, then came back with a different boot_id (096fd12c-..., matching the fixed after-executor snapshot). Post-restart, tree remained installed, /srv/localrepo files were intact, and httpd was restarted and confirmed serving HTTP 200 again.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract were directly satisfied: node1 served a local package repository from /srv/localrepo via busybox-extras httpd, remote repository unreachability was directly demonstrated (not just asserted), the `tree` package was successfully installed from the local repo while remotes were blocked, and the simulated outage was cleanly reversed. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated, with boot-identity change cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart recovery of the installed package, repo data, and served index.
limitations: The httpd process serving the local repo is not configured to auto-start on boot, so post-reboot service recovery required a manual restart command rather than being observed as automatic — acceptable since boot-time persistence was not part of the stated task, but noted for completeness.
Minor /tmp residue (httpd.log, httpd.pid, reboot.log) was left in place after the executor's final actions; low severity given it is scratch/log data in /tmp, not managed application state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Minor, low-risk residue: an early failed `busybox httpd` foreground attempt (cmd-c4e0d6e9a5464374) and pid/log files it wrote to /tmp were superseded without cleanup, and a subsequent failed `apk add` attempt against a wrong repository path (cmd-5f88c5346b4c4507) was a legitimate corrective iteration toward the install goal rather than an unrelated experiment, with no lasting package-state damage per the post-executor package-health check. Leftover /tmp/httpd.log, /tmp/httpd.pid, and /tmp/reboot.log files remained after the executor finished (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) — bounded, non-destructive residue in a scratch directory. The busybox-extras httpd process is not configured to persist across reboot (it had to be manually restarted post-reboot), which is an acceptable implementation choice since the task did not require boot-time persistence, but is noted as a residual manual step.
